title: fix(aws-lambda): respect backpressure when streaming the response body

questions.q: `streamHandle` calls `awslambda.streamifyResponse` without importing anything. What supplies `awslambda`, and what is `responseStream`?
questions.correct: A global from Lambda's Node runtime; `responseStream` is a Node `Writable`
distractors: A polyfill inside Hono's adapter; `responseStream` wraps the app's `Response`
API Gateway injects it per request; `responseStream` is the raw TCP socket
questions.diagram:
flowchart TD
  G["Lambda runtime: global awslambda"]:::hit
  G --> F["Hono: app.fetch(req)"]
  F --> B["res.body: web ReadableStream"]
  B -->|"pipeline()"| W["responseStream: Node Writable"]
  W --> R["Lambda runtime streams it out"]
  classDef hit stroke:#e8590c,stroke-width:3px
questions.why: The Lambda Node runtime defines `awslambda` as a global and hands the handler a Node `Writable`; the test fakes both with `vi.stubGlobal`. That is why the body must be bridged from a web stream to a Node stream at all.

questions.q: After this PR, a body finishes cleanly. Which call actually ends `responseStream`, and what does the `finally` block's `end()` do?
questions.correct: `pipeline` ends it once the generator returns; the later `end()` is a no-op
distractors: `readWebStream` ends it after its last `yield`; `pipeline` only paces reads
Only the `finally` block's `end()` does; `pipeline` never calls `end()`
The Lambda runtime ends it when the handler's promise resolves
questions.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant P as pipeline
  participant W as stream
  P->>W: write per yield
  P->>W: end() after last yield
  W-->>P: finish
  Note over P: resolves the handler
  Note over W: finally end(): no-op
questions.why: `pipeline` ends the destination when the source is exhausted and resolves only on `finish`. The `finally` call then hits a finished stream, which Node ignores when no callback is passed. `readWebStream` only yields; it never sees the writer.

questions.q: `res.body` is 2 MiB and the Lambda stream's `write()` returns `false` after the first chunk. What does this code do next?
questions.correct: The generator waits at `yield`; no `reader.read()` until `drain`
distractors: Keeps reading and writing; chunks pile up in the writable's buffer
Keeps reading; chunks queue inside the web stream until `drain`
Drops chunks until `drain`, then resumes with the next chunk read
questions.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant P as pipeline
  participant W as stream
  Note over P: generator yields chunk 1
  P->>W: write() is false
  Note over P: generator paused at yield
  W-->>P: drain
  Note over P: next() reads chunk 2
questions.why: `pipeline` pulls the generator only when the destination has room, so `reader.read()` waits for `drain`. The first option is exactly the pre-PR loop, which ignored `write()`'s return value.

questions.q: Why route the body through `pipeline` instead of keeping the loop and awaiting `'drain'` whenever `write()` returns `false`?
questions.correct: Awaiting `drain` paces writes but still resolves before `finish`
distractors: Lambda's `HttpResponseStream` never emits `drain`, so the loop would hang
`pipeline` coalesces small chunks, which cuts Lambda's per-write billing
`drain` needs Node 20, while `pipeline` runs on older Lambda runtimes
questions.diagram:
flowchart TD
  S["write() returns false"] --> A["loop awaits drain"]
  S --> P["pipeline(generator, writer)"]:::hit
  A --> A1["end(), resolve before finish"]
  P --> P1["resolve on finish"]
  P1 --> P2["errors destroy both sides"]
  classDef hit stroke:#e8590c,stroke-width:3px
questions.why: The bug had two halves: no pacing, and resolving after `end()` but before `finish`, which can end the invocation before delivery. A drain loop fixes only the first; `pipeline` also awaits `finish` and propagates errors from both ends.

questions.q: The body sends `chunk1;` and then errors. Before this PR the client got `chunk1;Internal Server Error`. What does it get now?
questions.correct: Just `chunk1;`: the stream is destroyed, so the catch block's write is lost
distractors: `chunk1;Internal Server Error`, as before; the catch block still writes
A 500 status with `Internal Server Error`, replacing the 200 response
Nothing at all: `pipeline` holds the body back and discards it on error
questions.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant P as pipeline
  participant W as stream
  P->>W: write chunk1;
  Note over P: body errors
  P->>W: destroy(err)
  Note over W: destroyed
  P->>W: catch: write ISE
  Note over W: dropped
questions.why: On error `pipeline` destroys the destination, and Node drops a `write()` or `end()` on a destroyed stream. The 200 already went out with the first bytes. The new test checks only that the handler logs and resolves, so this change passes unnoticed.

questions.q: A client disconnects from a `streamSSE` response and `responseStream` errors. What happens to the app's body stream?
questions.correct: Reads stop, but the body is never cancelled, so `onAbort` never fires
distractors: `pipeline` cancels the body, so `onAbort` callbacks run as usual
Reads continue to the end, filling the dead stream's internal buffer
The handler rejects, and Lambda retries the whole invocation
questions.diagram:
flowchart TD
  C["client disconnects"] --> W["responseStream errors"]
  W --> P["pipeline rejects"]
  P --> G["generator dropped at yield"]
  G --> X["reader.cancel() never called"]:::hit
  X --> Y["StreamingApi.abort() never runs"]
  classDef hit stroke:#e8590c,stroke-width:3px
questions.why: `readWebStream` has no `finally` that calls `reader.cancel()`, so the body stays locked and its `cancel` hook, the only path to `abort()`, never runs. Backpressure does stop the reads; reading on was the old loop.
